As of 550 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...High pressure builds across the region today leading 
to mainly dry and cool conditions today. 

Early this morning, a mid/upper-level trough is located along the 
mid-Atlantic coast and will close off just offshore of the OBX this 
morning. Meanwhile, 1030+ mb surface high pressure will continue to 
build in from the northwest allowing for clear and cool conditions 
for much of the FA. Breezy conditions will continue today, 
especially along the coast, but winds will be less than yesterday. 
Expect sunny to mostly sunny skies today for a majority of the area, 
with partly sunny skies across the far E/SE. Despite the full 
sunshine, high temperatures today are only expected to top out in 
the upper 50s to lower 60s. Clear and chilly conditions continue 
inland tonight with lows dipping back into the upper 30s for 
locations west of I-95, lower 40s around metro Richmond, and upper 
40s to mid 50s closer to the coast. Similar to this morning, frost 
formation is not expected due to a light breeze. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Breezy N to NE winds, and potentially unsettled 
conditions, are expected through the middle of next week along the 
immediate coast.

Developing low pressure meanders offshore between the mid 
Atlantic coast and Bermuda while 1030 mb high pressure remains 
anchored north of the area. 00z model guidance, mainly the 3k 
NAM and HRRR, continues to show outer rain bands and moisture 
rotating around the western periphery of the low back toward the
coast Monday into Tuesday. Slight chance to chance PoPs (~20 to
50%) are in the forecast for NE NC, Hampton Roads, and the 
Eastern Shore, while central VA and the Piedmont remain mostly 
dry with partly cloudy skies. With the low lingering offshore 
and high pressure to our north, persistent breezy conditions 
inland and prolonged windy conditions are expected along the 
immediate coast. N-NE gusts will average 20 to 25 mph inland and
30 to 45+ mph along the coast, highest over the Virginia Capes 
south to the NC Northern Outer Banks. A Wind Advisory is in 
effect for Eastern Currituck County through Monday night and the
City of Virginia Beach on Monday. Ensemble consensus indicates 
the low will begin a slow east- northeast drift further out to 
sea by midweek. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...A long-duration coastal flood event is expected.
Coastal Flood Watches are in effect from Monday through early 
Wednesday morning across the lower Chesapeake Bay, lower James 
River, and the Atlantic coast.

Model guidance continue to exhibit spread regarding a Nor'easter
lingering offshore early this week with respect to intensity 
and placement, particularly beyond Tuesday. With the cutoff low 
detached from the primary jet stream and lacking an upstream 
kicker trough, probabilistic ensembles favor a system meandering
offshore through midweek. Gusty N-NE winds will drive building 
tidal anomalies over the next few days.

Prolonged onshore flow will drive anomalies to 1 to 3 feet 
above normal astronomical tide. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help to
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides into the
middle of the week. If the low strengthens or edges closer to 
the coast, localized major flooding cannot be ruled out, though 
most guidance continues to trend "lower" toward high-end minor 
to moderate thresholds. Additionally, the latest model guidance
shows tidal levels continuing to gradually increase into Wed
with gradually higher tidal levels each day. For now, have
issued a Coastal Flood Advisory along the lower James River as
well as Virginia Beach and eastern Currituck. While more
marginal than yesterday's high tide, nuisance to minor coastal
flooding is expected with this afternoon's high tide across this
region. Not every location will reach minor flood stage.
However, with Smithfield and Fort Monroe favored to reach minor
flood stage as well as factoring in that a few non-forecast 
sites around Norfolk and Virginia Beach are trending higher than
nearby TWL sites and will likely reach minor flood stage, have 
gone ahead and included that whole region for the advisory.
Otherwise, have extended the Coastal Flood Watch through early 
Wed morning given the gradually increasing tides.
